svg.aria-label: Diagram: AWS Firewall Manager applies policies automatically as accounts and resources enter a policy scope, but leaving scope is not the mirror image. By default, a resource that goes out of scope remains associated and protected unless the customer selects the check box that automatically removes protections from resources that leave the policy scope, and that option is not available for AWS Shield Advanced or AWS WAF Classic policies. Three behaviours ignore the check box entirely: the associated AWS Config managed rules are deleted, any associated web ACLs that contain no resources are deleted, and the logging configuration is deleted regardless of the resource cleanup option value when a member account leaves the scope or when the policy is deleted. Those two triggers are narrower than the protections default, which covers an account or resource, and the cited page does not extend the logging rule to every resource-level scope change. For the two named events the state nobody chooses is a protection still enforcing with its logging gone. Deleting a policy also leaves things behind: replica security groups remain and require manual management in each Amazon VPC instance unless the clean-up option is chosen, and accounts remain subscribed to Shield Advanced after a Shield Advanced policy is deleted. On managed network ACL remediation, Firewall Manager only remediates network ACLs tagged FMManaged true, it needs space in the network ACL for interim rules and halts remediation when it hits the rule limit, and when an account's custom rules interfere it stops remediation and reports the conflict unless forced remediation is enabled.
svg.title: The protection stays; the logging goes
svg.text: Entry is automatic. Exit is opt-in. Three things ignore the setting.
AWS Firewall Manager — policy scope, resource cleanup, and what deleting a policy does not delete.
ENTERING SCOPE — no decision needed
“Firewall Manager automatically assesses it
against your settings for each policy and applies
the policy based on these settings.”
And “manages them continuously” thereafter.
LEAVING SCOPE — nothing happens by default
“doesn’t automatically remove protections or
delete Firewall Manager-managed resources
unless you select the … check box”
Not available for Shield Advanced or WAF Classic.
What the check box reaches, and what it does not
DEFAULT a protected resource “remains associated and protected” → the protection outlives the policy
SELECTED “automatically disassociated and removed from” protection → the resource is left bare
Both are defensible. Neither looks wrong six months later, which is why the choice belongs in writing.
Deleted regardless of the check box
“…the logging configuration regardless of
resource cleanup option value when a member

text.tspan: account leaves the scope or when the policy

svg.text: is deleted”
AWS Config managed rules — deleted
Web ACLs with no resources — deleted
For those two events, the state nobody chose:
still enforcing, no longer recording.
Deleting the policy leaves things behind
Security group policy, without the clean-up option:
“the replicas remain and require manual
management in each Amazon VPC instance”
Shield Advanced policy: “the policy is deleted, but
your accounts remain subscribed”
A cost that outlives the thing that created it.
Central remediation defers to the member account, unless you forced it
Custom rules interfere → “Firewall Manager stops any remediation activities on the network ACL” and reports it.
Forced remediation on → “applies the remediation, in spite of the conflict”. Off → “halts remediation”.
Only network ACLs with the FMManaged tag set to true · interim rules need free slots · at the rule limit it halts
Rule headroom stops being a capacity concern and becomes a precondition for the control working.
The audit: web ACLs in member accounts that no policy covers.
Under the default that set is non-empty in any organisation that has ever narrowed a scope, and each member is a
protection still enforcing whose logging went when the account left. Then look for Shield Advanced subscriptions with no policy.
Firewall Manager is eager on the way in and cautious on the way out. Most of the surprises are the cost of that caution.
